title: Hardik Pandya's Gujarat Titans Return Falls Through Over Captaincy Demand
excerpt: The all-rounder reportedly wanted to rejoin his former franchise but insisted on leading the side, a non-starter with Shubman Gill as GT's settled captain.
body:
• Hardik Pandya reportedly explored a return to Gujarat Titans ahead of IPL 2027 but insisted on captaincy, a demand the franchise rejected with Shubman Gill as their settled leader.
  • Seven of ten IPL franchises have expressed interest in trading for Pandya, with Kolkata Knight Riders and Rajasthan Royals furthest along in talks with Mumbai Indians.
  • Mumbai Indians finished ninth in IPL 2026 under Pandya's captaincy, with the all-rounder managing just 206 runs in 10 innings and four wickets at an economy of 11.43.
  • The IPL trade window closes ahead of the IPL 2027 mini auction in December, and any deal requires sign-off from both franchises and the player.

Hardik Pandya wanted to return to Gujarat Titans ahead of IPL 2027 but saw his proposed move collapse after the franchise rejected his demand for captaincy, the Hindustan Times reported. The all-rounder's insistence on leading the side proved a non-starter — Shubman Gill is GT's established captain, and the management has no interest in changing that arrangement.

Why the Gujarat Titans Deal Fell Apart

A return to Gujarat would have reunited Pandya with familiar faces from the franchise's first two seasons, during which he led GT to an IPL title in their debut year in 2022 and to the final in 2023. But as the Indian Express reported, Pandya sought to return with a "captaincy rider" — and the franchise said no.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=-fo0RB4btSg

Former India opener Aakash Chopra questioned the logic of the move. "He went from the Gujarat Titans only. Why would you want to go down that route? Shubman Gill is doing captaincy. Why would you assemble two alphas in this team?" Chopra said on his YouTube channel.

"I never doubted myself when it comes to leadership. It was always about knowing that I am a leader, knowing that I have the power and presence in any team that I play, where all 11 players will follow me if asked."

— Hardik Pandya, speaking to SGTV

Seven Franchises in the Hunt

With the GT return off the table, Pandya's departure from Mumbai Indians now appears to be a matter of when, not if. As many as seven franchises have approached MI about a trade, according to multiple reports, with Kolkata Knight Riders and Rajasthan Royals understood to be the most serious contenders.

https://x.com/Bhaveshlivelife/status/2087569868229157332

KKR's interest is tied specifically to leadership. The franchise has gone without a settled long-term captain since Shreyas Iyer's title-winning stint in 2024, and Ajinkya Rahane's two-year tenure produced two missed playoffs. An IPL insider told DNA India that "real discussions are happening" between KKR and MI after initial talks were delayed by the Reliance AGM.

Rajasthan Royals have reportedly floated a swap involving opener Yashasvi Jaiswal, but their pitch carries a complication. The franchise sees Riyan Parag as their long-term captain, meaning Pandya would likely arrive without the armband in Jaipur — a factor that could weigh heavily given his leadership ambitions.

A Disappointing Mumbai Tenure

Pandya's return to Mumbai Indians from Gujarat Titans in late 2023 was the biggest trade in IPL history, but results never matched expectations. He was immediately handed the captaincy in place of Rohit Sharma, a move that triggered fierce backlash from MI fans and never fully settled.

In three seasons as MI captain, Pandya guided the team to the playoffs only once — reaching Qualifier 2 in 2025 before losing to Punjab Kings. In IPL 2026, MI finished ninth in the ten-team table with just four wins from 14 games. Pandya himself struggled with both bat (206 runs at 22.89) and ball (four wickets at an economy of 11.43).

The 32-year-old is currently out of the Indian team due to fitness issues and has relocated to Bengaluru to train near the BCCI's Centre of Excellence. Selectors have indicated he will only be considered for ODI matches going forward to keep him fresh for the 2027 World Cup.

What's Next

IPL trade rules require sign-off from both franchises and the player, with any deal needing to be finalized before the window closes ahead of the IPL 2027 mini auction in December. With Gujarat Titans out of the picture, the race narrows to KKR's captaincy offer versus Rajasthan's talented squad — with at least five other franchises waiting in the wings.
